Let d,N be natural numbers with N>0. Let (Omega,m) be a measurable space, P a probability measure on it, and F a filtration indexed by nonnegative real time and subordinate to m. Write S={x in R^d: ||x||=1}, with its ordinary Euclidean coordinates. For each i in Fin N, let B_i:[0,infinity) x Omega -> R^d satisfy the supplied standard-Brownian-with-filtration predicate: B_i(0,omega)=0 for every omega; every finite collection of increments over pairwise disjoint half-open intervals (s_j,t_j] with s_j<=t_j is independent; for s<t and every continuous real linear functional ell, ell(B_i(t)-B_i(s)) has centered Gaussian law with variance (t-s)||ell||^2; sample paths are continuous P-almost surely; B_i is strongly adapted; and its increment from s to t, s<=t, is independent of F_s. No independence between different i is imposed. The exact measurable-space binding in the printed strong-adaptation predicate is one of the requested clarifications.

Assume the supplied SatisfiesUsualConditions predicate U(F,P): it contains right continuity of F and, for each t and set A with P(A)=0, a MeasurableSet A assertion. The pretty-print does not determine whether this assertion uses m or F_t. No stronger interpretation of that field is made here.

Let X_i,Y_i:[0,infinity) x Omega -> S be jointly measurable and satisfy the supplied IsStronglyProgressive F predicate. Its exact restricted-time domain/product measurable-space binding is not printed and is requested as a clarification. Let b_X,b_Y:[0,infinity) x S^N x S^N x Fin N -> R^d be such that, for each particle i, (t,x,y) -> b_X(t,x,y,i) and (t,x,y) -> b_Y(t,x,y,i) are jointly continuous. Let lambda be a nonnegative real number.

For every T>0, assume that P-almost surely, simultaneously for every nonnegative t<=T, every i in Fin N and every k in Fin d, both coordinate identities hold:
 X_i^k(t)=X_i^k(0)+int_0^t [b_X^k(s,X(s),Y(s),i)-lambda(d-1)X_i^k(s)] ds + sum_{j in Fin d} I_T(eta^X_{i,k,j},B_i^j)(t),
 Y_i^k(t)=Y_i^k(0)+int_0^t [b_Y^k(s,X(s),Y(s),i)-lambda(d-1)Y_i^k(s)] ds + sum_{j in Fin d} I_T(eta^Y_{i,k,j},B_i^j)(t).
Here X(s)=(X_l(s))_l, Y(s)=(Y_l(s))_l, B_i^j(s,omega) is exactly the j-th coordinate of B_i(s,omega), and both equations use that SAME scalar driver for each i,j. The integrands are exactly eta^Z_{i,k,j}(s,omega)=sqrt(2 lambda)[1_{k=j}-Z_i^j(s,omega)Z_i^k(s,omega)], for Z=X or Y. They are packaged as progressive L2 integrands over P times the time measure upTo(T). The drift integral is literally the integral against upTo(t), defined as the comap under inclusion [0,infinity)->R of Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,t].

I_T is the supplied itoIntegralProcess representative with the displayed horizon, probability measure, filtration and scalar Brownian driver. Its given body is zero on the complement of uniformCauchyEvent and otherwise the atTop limUnder of canonicalItoProcess approximants. Those approximants call canonicalElementaryApprox and elementaryItoProcess. The definitions of those two calls, uniformBadEvent, and terminalRepresentative, or equivalent identifying characterizations, are absent. The supplied zero-time, terminal-representative equality and martingale facts do not by themselves identify I_T with the standard L2 Ito integral. Accordingly that identification is unresolved here, rather than inferred from its name.

For real t let t_+=max(t,0), interpreted as a nonnegative real, and define
 delta_i(t,omega)=X_i(t_+,omega)-Y_i(t_+,omega),
 D(t)=N^{-1} sum_i int_Omega ||delta_i(t,omega)||^2 dP(omega),
 R4(t)=N^{-1} sum_i int_Omega ||delta_i(t,omega)||^4 dP(omega),
 L(t)=2 N^{-1} sum_i int_Omega <delta_i(t,omega),b_X(t_+,X(t_+,omega),Y(t_+,omega),i)-b_Y(t_+,X(t_+,omega),Y(t_+,omega),i)>_R dP(omega),
 G(t)=L(t)-2 lambda(d-3)D(t)-lambda R4(t).
All d-1 and d-3 terms are subtractions after casting d to the reals, not truncated natural-number subtraction.

The theorem concludes the conjunction: G:R->R is continuous; G is locally Lebesgue integrable on R; for every a,b>=0, D(b)-D(a)=int_a^b G(t)dt, with the oriented interval integral and no a<=b restriction; D is absolutely continuous on [0,T] for every nonnegative T; for every real t>0, D has classical derivative G(t) at t; and D has within-[0,infinity) derivative G(0) at zero. This does not assert that the derivative of the clamped extension equals G at negative times. There is no asserted process existence, equality of initial states, drift tangency, restriction d>0/d>=2, independence across particles, or additional numerical constant. The horizon-wise almost-sure event need not be one common event for all real horizons in the stated quantifier order.
